questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: one of the crucial aspects was the relevance and my own interests in the courses available at my destination and further that the city i was going to was a city i wanted to live in for a while

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: it has been a really nice stay and i have gotten to know many great people across the world. I further liked the courses i ended up with

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: some of the information, as for instance information about the university i was going to study at, was easy, but it was difficult to find practical information about registration and housing

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: i did not get any, except for the intro week at the university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: the students was at great help, but the exchange people were difficult to get in touch with in rotterdam

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: i was quite lucky finding a place, cause i have heard it should be difficult. it should be noted that it is not easy and it takes time and consistency

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: i would not say that there is a big difference, but having a roommate is a matter of course, as the prices in the netherlands a quite high as in copenhagen

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: before i could even apply they told us that the student housing were unavailable

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: they were difficult to get in touch with and had a long reply time

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: we had to get a registration form with practical information and signatures, but as they didn't reply quickly (the same with our own university at home) there was some missing signatures that made the process really long and confusing

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: only e mails were available

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i succeeded in getting them all approved, although the host university switched one of my courses to a "mandatory course" in the middle of the semester without warning, which i did not like. further the host university did not have any contact with my own university about this

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: i will say to start in good time, as the process and communication can take a lot of time, and it happens that they demand a resend which u will have to make time for within the deadlines

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: i liked my courses, although the level of education was not as i expected it would be. The level was quite low compared to what i am used to at home

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the assignment levels and study levels were just fine, but the level of general teaching and organization was lower than what i am used to

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: they took more use of "hands-on" assignments and group assignments which i did like, although the level of information given to the groups was low and confusing. they further had guest lectures a lot which made the courses more interesting

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
digital content
international journalism
feeling orange
media campaigns
digital maketing
international and global communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i really enjoyed international and global communication, as the teacher was really good and the topics were relevant and interesting. I further enjoyed media campaigns as it was very "hands-on" and we ended up with actual campaigns, which i think was awesome

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: going on trips to different parts of the country and other countries costs extra, of course and withdrawing cash if u dont have a dutch bank account/card

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: grocery shopping and food in general are cheaper than what i expected, but going to other cities was more expensive that expected. Also to go out /nightlife is more expensive as you pay quite a lot for entrance and wardrobe

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have a lot of fun places to go out, but i was missing some places still that had more of my own interests. Further i missed things to see in general in rotterdam, thus i went to see other cities in the netherlands

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: many bars and clubs and a couple of modern museums as well

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i would recommend "depot" which is a modern museum and just to google food places, as there is a lot of great food places from all around the world! Further if people like going for beers there are some really nice jazz clubs and nightclubs as well (mostly techno)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: what i mentioned above and go for some vintage shopping, rotterdam has many really nice ones!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it was easy, as the dutch culture is a lot like the danish culture, although you should be a bit carefull if you are not used to bike, as they have some funny route systems down here

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: the intro week is a good foundation for getting to know people, so i suggest you go! further just to meet people at bars and clubs, as Rotterdam is student city, so there are many young people from all around the world who wants to meet new people too

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The biking is a bit different due to their bike route and car/tram systems. Otherwise, it is the same as in Denmark

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: i like how friendly people are in general to exchange students in the city, as Rotterdam is a student city

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
plan some trips to some of the other cities close by, it is worth it, they are really beautiful.
take the bike or walk around so you see as much of the city as possible, because there are some really nice neighborhoods in Rotterdam and cafes too, just not in the city center.
as Rotterdam got bombed during the second world war the city center is really modern and has a lack of charm, but if you just go a bit to the north or west, you will find beautiful places!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: not except for above mentioned

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: to meet all these great people and to try and live in another country for a while. I will recommend it a lot!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: struggling with bills, because i did not know that having a dutch card/dutch bank was so important in order to pay rent, telephone bills etc...

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: that was it I would say

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
